# Section 040: Automation and Tooling

Makes the reader able to run and read the three kinds of security automation that keep a cluster compliant after the initial setup: configuration scanning with Trivy, policy enforcement at admission with Kyverno and ValidatingAdmissionPolicy, and runtime detection with Falco rules. It teaches what each kind can and cannot prove, how a finding turns into a fix or a recorded exception, and how control drift appears when the cluster and its approved source differ.

**Curriculum item covered:** Automation and Tooling

---

## What You Will Master

- Compare configuration scanning, policy enforcement and runtime detection by decision point and by what each leaves unproven
- Read a finding through its target, tool version, rule and effective behavior
- Run a Trivy misconfiguration scan on live Deployments and read the check ID, severity and cause
- Fix a finding in the cluster and prove the fix on the running pod, not only on the template
- Record an exception with a reason, a scope, an owner, a compensating control and an expiry date
- Keep scan evidence with its time, target, tool version and a checksum
- Explain control drift and repair it against an approved source
- Write a Kyverno ClusterPolicy, compare `Audit` and `Enforce`, and read a PolicyReport
- Write a ValidatingAdmissionPolicy and a binding, and choose between `Deny`, `Warn` and `Audit`
- Read a Falco rule (condition, output, priority, macros and lists) and reason about the events it matches

## The Learning Path

### 1. Automation, Findings And Control Drift
*   **Module Reader:** **[Module 1: Automation, Findings And Control Drift](./module-01/course.md)**
*   **Hands-on Playground:** `sections/section-040/module-01/playground` — kind cluster, no policy engine. Namespaces `starfleet` and `outpost` with the Starfleet workloads (`scout` without a securityContext, `probe` with a privileged container, `shuttle` that writes to its root file system, `drifter` in outpost). A Trivy 0.76.1 toolbox pod and an empty exception register in `tools`.
    ```bash
    astrona run --git ssh://git@github.com/astrona-io/ATS046.git -c sections/section-040/module-01/playground
    ```

### 2. Policy Enforcement And Runtime Detection
*   **Module Reader:** **[Module 2: Policy Enforcement And Runtime Detection](./module-02/course.md)**
*   **Hands-on Playground:** `sections/section-040/module-02/playground` — kind cluster with Kyverno 1.19.1 installed and no policy. The Starfleet workloads run in `starfleet` and `outpost`; `probe` is privileged and no Deployment has an `owner` label. Falco is taught by reading and is not installed.
    ```bash
    astrona run --git ssh://git@github.com/astrona-io/ATS046.git -c sections/section-040/module-02/playground
    ```

### Section Capstone Challenge
*   **Comprehensive Challenge:** Automation and Tooling Capstone — `sections/section-040/capstone/labs/lab-01`
    ```bash
    astrona run --git ssh://git@github.com/astrona-io/ATS046.git -c sections/section-040/capstone/labs/lab-01
    astrona submit -c .
    ```
*   **Hands-on Objective:** One turn of a continuous compliance loop. The reader scans with Trivy, fixes the privileged `probe`, repairs a hand-made `hostNetwork` drift on `scout` against the approved manifest, enforces privileged containers with a Kyverno policy, denies host network Deployments with a ValidatingAdmissionPolicy, and records a dated exception for `shuttle`. The grader checks the running pods, tests rejections with server-side dry runs and reads the exception register.
